text: Many great and wise teachings have been handed down to us in the Scriptures, that is, in the Law, the Prophets, and the other writings.[1] We should praise earlier generations of Israel for writing and saving these books. And if you really love to study the Scriptures, it is very important for you to be able to explain them to others, whether by talking or by writing. That's why my grandfather Jesus studied the Scriptures until he became an expert, then wrote this book to help others learn about wisdom. So if you love to learn, you should study this book, and you will come closer and closer to living as the Law requires. But I ask you to read with a good attitude and not to be critical of my translation. I worked hard at it, so be understanding in those places where it isn't perfect. The meaning of any Hebrew book changes a little when it is translated, whether it is from the Law or the Prophets or is one of the other books in the Scriptures. I came to Egypt in the thirty-eighth year of King Euergetes, and I stayed there for as long as he was king.[2] While I was there, I studied copies of many books, and that's when I realized I should translate this one. Translating carefully takes a lot of hard work, and I spent many sleepless nights before my translation was completed. And now that it is finished, those who live outside of Judea can read this book to learn how best to obey God's Law in their own lives. Only the Lord can give Wisdom, and his Wisdom lasts forever.
And who but the Lord can count the raindrops or the days in eternity or the sand on the seashore?
And who else can measure the height of heaven or the width of the earth or the depth of the sea?
The Lord created Wisdom long before anything else.
The Wisdom in God's commands flows from his word in heaven like streams from a spring.[3]
Who can understand the deep thoughts of Wisdom or how clever she[4] is?
Can anyone be taught all of her knowledge? Can anyone understand how much she has learned?[5]
Only the Lord is that wise; he is fearsome and majestic as he rules from his throne.
The Lord created Wisdom and watched her grow, then he gave her to his creation—
to every living thing— but especially to those people who love him.[6]
If you fear the Lord, you will be proud of the honors you receive, and you will wear happiness like a crown.
And if you fear him, your life will be long and filled with joy.[7]
You will die happy, blessed by the Lord on the day of your death.
Respect and obey the Lord— that's where Wisdom begins, and she will stay with faithful people from the day of their birth.
She has lived among us humans since the beginning of time, and she will never desert our descendants.
Respect and obey the Lord— this is complete Wisdom. Be drunk on the wine of Wisdom,
and let her fill your house and your barns with the harvest she brings.
Wisdom will give you respect for the Lord, to be worn like a crown woven from the flowers of peace and good health.[8]
Hold on to Wisdom, and she will honor you by sending knowledge and complete understanding like showers of rain.
Wisdom is like a tree— at its root is respect for the Lord, and its branches represent a long lifetime.
Fear of the Lord forces sin and anger out of your life.[9]
It is never right to be angry without a good reason, because anger will start you down the path to disaster.
Just be patient and stay calm until your anger fades.
Then when the time is right you can speak, and others will tell of your good sense.
Wisdom collects wise sayings, but faithfulness to God is disgusting to a sinner.
If you want lots of Wisdom from the Lord, then obey his commands.
Respect and obey the Lord, and you will learn Wisdom; be faithful and humble, and he will be pleased.
Faithfully obey the Lord and worship him with all your heart.
Others are watching you, so be careful— don't say one thing and then do something else.
If you boast and then fail, you will be disgraced. And if you only pretend to worship the Lord, he will bring you down and show everyone that you are a fake.
